item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 271125
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM EDT Sun Sep 27 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Depression Fay, located well to the west-southwest of the Azores.

Central Subtropical Atlantic:
A surface trough of low pressure located several hundred miles east
of Bermuda continues to produce an area of disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. Environmental conditions appear somewhat favorable
for gradual development of this system, and a tropical depression
could form by the early to mid portion of this week as it initially
moves northward before turning eastward early this week over the
central Subtropical Atlantic.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...30 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

$$
Forecaster Papin
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.description:
Issued at 300 PM GMT Sun Sep 27 2026

BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Fay Advisory Number  30
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 PM GMT Sun Sep 27 2026
 
...FAY DRIFTING SOUTH-SOUTHEASTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM GMT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...29.3N 43.8W
ABOUT 1135 MI...1825 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...SSE OR 160 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1010 MB...29.83 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM GMT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Fay was
located near latitude 29.3 North, longitude 43.8 West. The
depression is moving toward the south-southeast near 3 mph (6 km/h). 
A slow turn to the south-southwest to southwest is forecast on 
Tuesday followed by a turn toward the west-southwest with an 
increase in forward speed by mid-week.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast over the next several days.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1010 mb (29.83 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Roberts

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Forecast Discussion Number 30
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM GMT Sun Sep 27 2026 
485 
WTNT41 KNHC 271439
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Depression Fay Discussion Number  30
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 PM GMT Sun Sep 27 2026
 
This morning's GOES-19 Proxy-VIS satellite presentation indicates 
that Fay's cloud pattern has changed little since yesterday, and 
the TAFB subjective satellite intensity estimate supports 30 kt for 
this advisory.
 
Modest northerly shear continues to impinge on the north side of
the cyclone, displacing the small pulsating deep bursts of 
convection just to the south of the surface center.  The GFS/ECMWF 
statistical SHIPS intensity guidance indicates little change in the 
shear pattern and magnitude and the thermodynamic environment 
through mid-week.  Therefore, the NHC forecast shows Fay 
maintaining depression strength during the next few days.  There is 
growing confidence due to deterministic and AI-single model 
agreement indicating that Fay will finally lose what little 
organized convection it has held onto, and eventually open up into 
a trough toward the end of the week.  The official intensity 
forecast follows this scenario and is based on the aforementioned 
SHIPS and the HFIP HCCA guidance.
 
Fay's initial motion is estimated to be south-southeastward, or 
160/3 kt.  Fay is forecast to move southwestward to 
west-southwestward around the southeastern peripheral low-level 
flow of a subtropical high located midway between Bermuda and the 
cyclone.  A few of the deterministic models indicate slight 
strengthening of the aforementioned ridge early in the period.  
Therefore, a slight increase in forward speed is indicated in the 
NHC forecast beyond Tuesday, and this agrees with the better 
performing consensus models.
